Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Do Eastern cultures have their own explorers who "found Europe" that they celebrate?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends play a game where you pretend to discover new places. In some stories, people from faraway lands (like from Asia or Africa) actually traveled to Europe a long, long time ago, even before people from Europe went to their lands.

But in most of the stories and celebrations in Eastern countries (like China, Japan, or India), people usually talk about their own explorers who went to other places, like the sea or nearby lands, not about “finding Europe.” They don’t usually have big celebrations for people who went to Europe first, because it was usually Europeans who went to Asia and other places first, not the other way around.

So, most Eastern cultures don’t have stories or celebrations about their own people “finding Europe” like some Western countries have about finding America. Instead, they have their own heroes who explored the seas or discovered things in their own part of the world.
